summary: This note is a long encyclopedic overview of human rights, covering their definition as inalienable, universal and egalitarian moral and legal entitlements, and their intellectual history from natural rights through the Enlightenment to the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948. It also surveys the main international treaties, UN and regional human rights bodies, and promotion strategies such as military force, economic sanctions and monitoring by NGOs. The text is cut off partway through its discussion of regional regimes in the Americas.
one_line: Overview of human rights as universal moral and legal entitlements, their history from natural rights to the UDHR, and the international institutions that protect them.
key_facts: Human rights are described as inalienable, fundamental rights "to which a person is inherently entitled simply because she or he is a human being."
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in 1948 in Paris.
The UDHR was adopted unanimously, with the abstention of the Soviet bloc, apartheid South Africa, and Saudi Arabia.
Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the Human Rights Commission that framed the UDHR, which began discussing an International Bill of Rights in 1947.
John Locke identified natural rights as "life, liberty, and estate (property)" and argued such rights could not be surrendered in the social contract.
Magna Carta was originally issued in 1215 and influenced the common law and later constitutional documents on human rights.
The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights were adopted by the UN in 1966 and came into force in 1976.
The UN Human Rights Council was created in 2005 and has 47 of the 193 UN member states sitting on it.
The International Criminal Court's Rome Statute established the court, which has a mandate over crimes occurring after its creation in 2002.
In 2022, the UN General Assembly passed a resolution declaring that everyone has a right to a healthy environment.
The League of Nations was established in 1919 at the negotiations over the Treaty of Versailles.
The African Union consists of fifty-five African states and was established in 2001.
The Organization of American States has thirty-five independent member states and is headquartered in Washington, D.C.
The Paris Principles were defined at a workshop in Paris on 7–9 October 1991 and adopted by UN resolutions in 1992 and 1993.

entities.name: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
entities.role: non-binding declaration adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1948, framed by the Human Rights Commission, that urges states to promote human, civil, economic and social rights

entities.name: United Nations General Assembly
entities.role: body that adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948 and elects members of the Human Rights Council

entities.name: Eleanor Roosevelt
entities.role: chair of the Human Rights Commission that framed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

entities.name: John Humphrey
entities.role: Canadian law professor responsible for much of the cross-national research for the UDHR (written as "John Humprey" in the note)

entities.name: René Cassin
entities.role: French lawyer who structured the UDHR document

entities.name: John Locke
entities.role: 17th century English philosopher who discussed natural rights as life, liberty and estate

entities.name: Mahatma Gandhi
entities.role: leader of the Indian independence movement, consulted in drafting the UDHR, and influential national liberation figure

entities.name: Henry David Thoreau
entities.role: wrote about human rights in his 1849 treatise On the Duty of Civil Disobedience

entities.name: Magna Carta
entities.role: English charter originally issued in 1215 that influenced the common law and later constitutional documents

entities.name: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights
entities.role: 1966 UN covenant making UDHR civil and political rights binding, in force from 1976

entities.name: International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
entities.role: 1966 UN covenant committing state parties to work toward economic, social and cultural rights, in force from 1976

entities.name: Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
entities.role: treaty establishing the International Criminal Court, which entered into force in 2002

entities.name: International Criminal Court
entities.role: body responsible for investigating and punishing war crimes and crimes against humanity within its jurisdiction

entities.name: International Court of Justice
entities.role: UN's primary judiciary body that settles disputes between nations and lacks jurisdiction over individuals

entities.name: United Nations Human Rights Council
entities.role: council created in 2005 to investigate alleged human rights violations, based in Geneva

entities.name: League of Nations
entities.role: established in 1919 after World War I with goals including disarmament and collective security

entities.name: International Labour Organization
entities.role: agency of the League of Nations, now part of the UN, with a mandate to promote decent work

entities.name: Amnesty International
entities.role: independent non-governmental organisation that monitors human rights abuses

entities.name: Human Rights Watch
entities.role: independent non-governmental organisation that monitors human rights abuses

entities.name: African Union
entities.role: continental union of fifty-five African states established in 2001 to secure democracy and human rights

entities.name: Organization of American States
entities.role: international organization of thirty-five independent states of the Americas, headquartered in Washington, D.C.

entities.name: Bolsa familia
entities.role: conditional cash transfer program that subsidizes parents who keep children in school and has reduced child labor

entities.name: Responsibility to protect
entities.role: doctrine for UN member states to intervene to protect populations from atrocities

entities.name: Cyrus Cylinder
entities.role: oldest cited evidence of human rights, dated to the 6th century BCE, with provisions on religion and racial equality
